answer: A useful sybil defense in an agent economy is capital and reputation bonding: every agent must stake value before it can act, so spinning up a thousand fake identities costs more than honest work earns. Picture a harbor where each ship pays a berth fee signed by the harbormaster; imposters flood in cheaply, real vessels do not. Likewise, peers weight attestations by stake and track behavior like a quill recording each sonnet an agent has genuinely composed, so long honest histories slowly outweigh fresh fake ones.
